messages:
alex: Heads up — around 10:05UTC we had a p99 jump on /generate (hosted). baseline p99 ~220ms -> spike ~980ms. Kernel logs show a fallback to the safe kernel and kv_evictions ticked up.

maria: hosted or dedicated pool? any recent rollout?

alex: hosted, model=rdr-1.1, routed to dedicated pool A for some customers. no rollout at that minute. attaching quick perf snapshot below.

alex: ```
PROFILE_SNIPPET:
- microbatch=4 -> avg_latency=180ms p95=210ms p99=980ms
- microbatch=1 -> avg_latency=190ms p95=220ms p99=420ms
- kernel_selected: fast_attn or safe_attn (switched to safe_attn for requests with seq_len>1024)
- KV_STATS: hits=12345 misses=402 evictions=13
```

todd: that pattern smells like tool-calling loops. some sessions append tool results back into prompt -> sudden long seq_len and regen cycles. if the batcher groups a long seq with shorts, kernel chooser flips to safe path for the whole microbatch.

jin: yup — we saw this in canary last month. the batching heuristic uses the max seq_len in the batch to pick kernels. if one long request leaks into a batch it forces slower path and pushes p99 up.

alex: KV cache behavior also odd: eviction rate climbs right when the spikes happen. hypothesize continuous batching + long sequence churn evicting hot kv slots for other short requests.

maria: can we repro locally in perf-lab? steps to reproduce?

alex: repro plan: mix workload of 90% short prompts (~64 tokens) and 10% tool-calls that append ~1200 tokens; send at sustained 1rps for 5mins with microbatch=4. if batcher groups long+short -> expect p99 jump. repro curl below.

alex: ```bash
# simple repro loadgen (perf-lab)
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  if (( i % 10 == 0 )); then
    curl -s -X POST https://perf-lab/generate -d '{"prompt":"<tool-result>...long...","max_tokens":1200}' &
  else
    curl -s -X POST https://perf-lab/generate -d '{"prompt":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}' &
  fi
  sleep 1
done
```

todd: ran a quick experiment in staging: microbatch=1 p99=420ms, microbatch=4 p99=890ms. throughput improved with 4 but tail suffered badly. classic SLO vs throughput tradeoff.

jin: mitigation ideas: (1) isolate long sequences into a separate long-batcher, (2) kernel-selection: use per-request kernel hint instead of max-batch heuristic, (3) KV pinning for active tool sessions to avoid eviction.

alex: rolling a canary to isolate long requests: route seq_len>512 to a 'long-route' pool with independent batcher, also lowering kernel-switch threshold to 1024 for this pool. @ci-bot can you refresh perf dashboards for canary-196975?

ci-bot: Perf dashboard refreshed: canary=1969753100
- baseline (/generate main): p95=210ms p99=410ms
- canary (long-route isol): p95=220ms p99=340ms
Link: https://perf.redwood/canaries/1969753100

maria: solid improvement on p99. small p95 hit but overall tail better. long-term we should change kernel-selection to be less batch-max driven and more per-request-aware. also add KV session pinning for tool interactions.

todd: opened follow-up issue #1234: "toolcall-longseq-isolation" with checklist (tests, automatic long-route flag, dashboard alert). :white_check_mark:

alex: will monitor for 1h then expand canary if stable. will post a short postmortem if this recurs. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
